Hi Suzanne — great to hear the demo landed well. Short answers up front: the residency uplift is a recurring surcharge tied to data residency (per-region capacity + compliance ops) and is typically modeled as a fixed monthly fee (not a % of compute) for production environments; for pilots we usually waive or heavily discount it. KMS/HSM is most commonly handled as a small annual license per HSM cluster plus a usage overlay for key ops when customers do high-volume encryption — we can offer a hybrid.

I’ve attached a simple pricing matrix that shows three pathways: pilot-waived residency + ramped residency fee, pilot-credit conversion (convert unused pilot discount into implementation credit), and a committed-residency plan with discounted annual KMS seats. I recommend the pilot-waive + 6-month amortized credit for your use-case.

Can we hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to align procurement and engineering? If you can share the procurement template (attached to your note) I’ll have our SOW and a one-page concession proposal ready.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Team — forwarding QuantaHealth’s procurement question. Key asks: avoid cliff after pilot; want clear path to production. My read: they’re smallish pilot (3mo, us-west), then scale to org-wide in month 7. Proposed internal approach:

- Waive residency uplift during 3-month pilot (no recurring residency fee).
- Offer KMS licensing at 40% off for first 12 months, then step-up to list over next 12 months (ramp: 40% -> 20% -> full).
- Convert any pilot discount not used into an implementation credit applied across first 6 invoices post-GA.

Open questions: seat vs throughput billing for KMS (I think hybrid is best). Need legal to sign off on credit language (cap credits to implementation fees). Also want to confirm whether we should require a 6- or 12-month minimum committed residency after GA to keep the concession. Thoughts?

—Jonas

Agree with the approach and will tighten the numbers. Proposed concession structure to present to QHS:

- Residency uplift: waived for pilot (3 months). If customer signs a 9-month committed residency within 90 days of pilot end, we backdate a pro-rated credit equal to 50% of the first 3 months’ estimated residency fee (applied across first 3 invoices).
- KMS/HSM: 45% off standard KMS seats for year 1 on any signed production contract; seats convert to list price in year 2 with a 12-month step-down schedule. For HSM clusters (if required), offer a 30% implementation credit to cover onboarding.
- Amortization: convert pilot discount into implementation credit and amortize over 6 invoices. Include an explicit clause: concession is conditional on a signed production MSA within 120 days of pilot completion.

I’ll draft the SOW language and include the cap on credits (so we don’t create open-ended liabilities). Sending a draft now.

—Lauren

Michael / Suzanne — appreciate the clarity — quick compromise proposal below (we want to keep commercial risk manageable while unlocking your approvals):

- Residency uplift: Waived for the 3-month pilot. On signature of production MSA within 120 days, Redwood will issue an up-front invoice credit equal to the waived residency fee (credit applied to first invoice). The credit is capped at the pilot-estimated residency fee (not to exceed $75k).
- KMS/HSM: Offer 45% discount on KMS seats for the first 12 months. For customers that require a true 60% concession, we can accommodate at a 12-month prepay or a 24-month commit (we're flexible).
- HSM clusters: 30% implementation credit applied on the first invoice (same cap mechanics).
- Contract terms: concession is conditional on signed MSA within 120 days of pilot end and a 12-month minimum residency commitment post-GA to avoid clawback.

If that looks acceptable I’ll update the SOW and route a DocuSign envelope with the concession language and SOW. If you prefer the 60% without prepay/commit, we’ll need a simple commercial addendum and a slightly higher cap.

Next steps: confirm preferred option today and we’ll send the DocuSign for signatures by EOD.
